summary: Clarify runtime state required for rollback after the start-operation upgrade

replay.detail: Documentation introduces no additional projection replay or recovery trigger.

schema.detail: No additional schema or storage-version change; this clarifies the separately classified version-19 upgrade.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or digest change.

compatibility.detail: No additional runtime or client protocol change. New operation-provenance generation records from the start-operation upgrade remain unreadable by older exec runtimes.

downtime.detail: The ordinary roll remains forward-only with an online SQLite snapshot and the separately classified normal restart. A requested swap-back cut requires a separately accepted per-member maintenance window that stops all owned runtimes and the daemon; it is not a routine pre-roll step.

manual.detail: Before swapping back, establish exact producer/runtime closure, quiesce the daemon and all listed writers, and capture SQLite plus only the explicitly inventoried exec/PTY generation and hashed scope records using the documented Python 3.9-compatible recipe. Preserve per-member roots privately; do not scan or copy runtime trees. The approved limitation is that unproven old PTY closure has no release command in this slice.

recovery.detail: Restore the matching pre-upgrade database, binary and explicitly captured generation/scope files together while quiesced; preserve the upgraded cut first. Missing preimages or unproved closure require roll-forward. Storage upgrades are rolled separately. Resolved ledger rows remain in claims.sqlite3 forever; the documented offline payload and disk measurements track admission-dependent growth.
